title: forager.yaml
description: The machine's forager.yaml, under the user's configuration directory alone: what qory run does on this machine. gateway holds the run policy's egress section, the server document, the credentials, the tools and the integrations; session holds the instance and what applies to every run; wall is the container the runtime is started in. egress and server follow the Forager contract's grammar, https://qory.dev/contracts/forager/v1/, and wall is that contract's wall.

machine.description: The adapter that made this machine, such as aws-ec2, or none. qory run passes it to Forager, which reports it as machine in dev.qory.run.started. Default unset: dev.qory.run.started has no machine.

gateway.description: The gateway's sections: the egress policy, the server, the credentials, the tools, the integrations, the memory lock and the run limits; and for qory gateway, listen and tls.

paths.description: The paths a run may request on a host, by host, as a policy's egress.paths. They apply to every run on this machine: a run's policy, from --policy or the server, keeps its path rules, and a request to a host either lists must match an entry of each that lists it. The proxy reads those hosts' requests, so every run on this machine needs a wall.

server.description: The server every run on this machine reports to, the Forager contract's server.schema.json without its version: Forager signs every request with the machine's access key, verifies every answer under the pin, fetches the server's configuration, posts the events where it defines and takes its run configuration. The access key's secret is never in this file: it is QORY_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET, else the file access-key-secret beside it. Absent, the events go to files alone.

url.description: https, or http to this machine; a scheme and a host with nothing after.

access_key_id.description: The id of the machine's access key, which the server assigns when the key enrols: ak_ and 16 characters of lower-case Crockford base32. May be left out when QORY_ACCESS_KEY_ID is set in the environment; set in both, it is refused. A run without one does not start.

apiary_public_key.description: The pin: the server's Ed25519 public keys, a list so the key can rotate. Every answer of the server is verified under one of them. May be left out when QORY_APIARY_PUBLIC_KEY holds it, as JSON; set in both, it is refused. A pin that lists the Forager contract's published fixture key is refused. A run without one does not start, apiary_public_key_missing.

public_key.description: A raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key, base64url without padding.

via.description: Optional: the gateway this machine reaches the server through, when that gateway is its only way out. Every request to the server goes to the gateway's address with its path unchanged, and the gateway passes it on and passes the answer back; url above stays the server's. The gateway's certificate chain is always checked. Absent, the server is reached directly.

url.description: The gateway: an https URL of a host and an optional port, with nothing after.

ca_file.description: A PEM file of the certificate authority that signed the gateway's certificate, when the system's roots do not hold it. qory reads it relative to forager.yaml's directory, and it takes the place of the system's roots for this connection.

certificate_sha256.description: Optional: the SHA-256 of the gateway certificate's public key, base64. With it, qory accepts only a certificate with that key, and still checks its chain.

enrolment_code_file.description: Optional, for qory gateway alone: the file Qory Apiary writes the gateway's enrolment code (qecg_) into, relative to forager.yaml's directory unless absolute. When qory gateway starts with no access key, it waits until the file exists, enrols with the code and writes access-key-secret. The path has no link in it, the file is regular, and only root and the user running qory may write it and its folders; a folder that root owns with the sticky bit set, such as /tmp, passes, since no other user may replace a file in it. qory never writes or removes it. qory run, qory run pool, qory run register and qory run end stop with an error when it is set.

credentials.description: The credentials this machine has for its runs, by name. A run's policy selects among them and defines none. Behind a wall the gateway keeps each outside the container and sets it on the requests to the hosts it is for, ending the container's TLS for those hosts alone. Exactly one of env, file and adapter defines where the token comes from. A model key has format, endpoint and auth in place of hosts, paths and placeholders.

env.description: A variable of qory run's environment that contains the token.

file.description: The absolute path of a file that contains the token, read again whenever it is used.

adapter.description: A program of yours, by its absolute path, and its arguments: it is written for one kind of host, such as a source code host, runs outside the container, and prints one JSON document, the Forager contract's credential.schema.json: the token, when it expires, and the hosts, the scheme and the paths it is for. ${argument} in an argument is replaced by the argument the run's policy defines. The gateway runs the adapter again before the token expires and when a host refuses it.

argument.description: A regular expression the policy's argument must match whole, with an adapter. Absent, a policy passes none.

hosts.description: With env or file, the hosts the token is for. With an adapter, the most it may claim.

paths.description: With env or file, the paths of the hosts the token goes to, and under enforce the only ones the run may request: a path matched whole or up to a final * as a prefix; absent is every path. With an adapter, the most it may claim.

auth.description: How the token is set: bearer, basic with a username, or header with a header's name. A credential from env or file needs it, and so does a model key from an adapter. Any other credential from an adapter takes none: the adapter's answer contains how its token is set.

oauth.description: For a model key with the scheme bearer: true marks the key as an OAuth token, such as a Claude subscription login's.

placeholders.description: Variables the container gets with a value that is no credential, for a program that does not start without one set; the proxy replaces what the program sends.

format.description: A model key's API format. The run's runtime gets the key in the variable it reads for this format and auth.

endpoint.description: A model key's base URL: https, a host, an optional port and path, and no user, query or fragment. The proxy sets the key on every path of this host alone, and the run's runtime gets this URL as its model endpoint.

key_prefixes.description: A model key's prefixes, such as sk-ant-: 1 to 4, each 1 to 32 characters of printable ASCII without a space. If the key starts with none of them, the run does not start. Without key_prefixes, any key is accepted.

tools.description: The tools this machine has for its runs, by name. A run's policy selects among them, with an argument, and defines none. Behind a wall the gateway starts each for the run, outside the container, and the proxy hands it the requests it allows to the hosts the tool serves.

command.description: A program of yours, by its absolute path, and its arguments. ${argument} in an argument is replaced by the argument the run's policy gives.

argument.description: A regular expression the policy's argument must match whole. Absent, a policy passes none.

serves.description: The hosts whose requests go to the tool, in egress.allow's grammar. A host need not exist: the proxy never dials it.

placeholders.description: Variables the container gets with a value that is no credential, for a program that does not start without one set.

integrations.description: The integrations this machine declares, by key: programs that speak the integration contract, https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/. qory runs <program> describe, checks the settings against the description, and expands each role it supports; the credential role defines the credential whose name is the key, unless gateway.credentials defines that name itself. An integration that plays no role qory expands is refused.

program.description: The program: an absolute path, or a name looked up on the PATH. Default qory-<key>. qory runs it from outside the checkout and outside every read-write mount of the wall's container, judged by where its links lead. The resolved program, every directory above it up to /, and every directory above each link on the way belong to root or the user running qory, and so does each link; other users may write none of them, except a directory root owns with the sticky bit set, which keeps the rule; a group may write one when it is root's (gid 0), wheel, admin, or the owner's primary group when its name is the owner's.

settings.description: The settings document, which the description's settings schema checks; absent is {}. It goes on the command line of every role, so it contains no value of a writeOnly setting: a secret is set through <setting>_file, the path of the file that contains it.

listen.description: The address qory gateway listens on for the runs of other machines, host:port. qory run never listens on it: it starts a gateway itself on a loopback port for each run.

tls.description: The certificate and key qory gateway serves the other machines with.

lock_memory.description: On Linux, true locks every page of the gateway's process in memory, so that no key it holds is written to swap. It needs RLIMIT_MEMLOCK unlimited, or the capability CAP_IPC_LOCK. On any other system, true stops the gateway. The default is false.

run_limits.description: The limits of each run on the gateway, the same for every run. A field left out is its default.

connections.description: The most connections a run has open at once. The default is 256.

requests_per_second.description: The requests a run sends a second. The default is 50.

burst.description: The requests a run sends at once after a pause. The default is 200.

stack_hosts.description: The hosts the stack proxy of each run on the gateway reaches, in egress.allow's grammar: a lower-case host name, an IPv4 address in canonical form or a *. suffix. The stack proxy is open until the run's session starts, and allows a listed host without the run's policy. Behind a wall or through a separate gateway, it reaches the gateway's machine or a private network address only for a host that this list and the allow list of the gateway's policy both list by name, and never a link-local or cloud metadata address. Absent or empty means the stack proxy reaches no host.

session.description: The session's sections: the instance and what applies to every run.

instance.description: This instance of the machine, as the server shows it. Its id is made by qory and kept in the file instance-id beside this file.

name.description: The instance's display name on the server: 1 to 64 of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dot, underscore and dash, starting with a letter or a digit. Default the host name.

run.description: What applies to every run on this machine unless a flag of qory run overrides it.

timeout.description: How long a runtime may run, as a duration: 5h30m. At the limit Forager stops it and dev.qory.run.exited reports the limit as the reason. Default no limit. --timeout sets another for one run. A run from a run code does not use it: it takes its time limit from Qory Apiary's response to the code, else from its workflow, else 3 hours.

stop_signal.description: The signal that requests a runtime to stop when Forager stops it, at the limit or on a signal to qory run. Runtimes differ in what a signal means, so the runtime's descriptor defines which, and this key sets another for every run on the machine. Default the descriptor's, and SIGTERM when it defines none. --stop-signal sets another for one run.

stop_grace.description: How long a runtime gets between the stop signal and SIGKILL when Forager stops it, at the limit or on a signal to qory run: the time a session needs to close what it has open. Default the runtime's descriptor's, and 10s when it defines none. --stop-grace sets another for one run.

wall.description: The wall every run on this machine starts the runtime behind: a container with no route out except to the gateway's proxy. Absent, the runtime is a process of this machine.

image.description: The agent's image when the run's policy selects none, the runtime and the project's toolchain: the name of one of images, or a reference. A name images defines is read as that image first. --image sets another for one run, and a policy's selection wins over both. May be left out when --image sets one, or when the run's --policy selects an image; a machine that reports to a server sets it, because the server's run configuration may select none.

images.description: The images this machine defines, by name. A run's policy selects one by its name, as it selects credentials, or names a reference only under images_allow; image and --image name the default by it. The Forager contract's Images.

ref.description: The image's reference, pinned by digest where the machine wants the same image every time.

runtime.description: The container runtime the wall starts the image under, one the engine has, such as sysbox-runc. Default the engine's.

docker.description: Experimental. Nested Docker, a Docker daemon inside the wall, separate from the machine's: qory's helper starts it before the agent; the image holds dockerd. Needs Docker Engine 28 or later and a runtime that runs a daemon without privileges: sysbox-runc. Any policy can select the image, so define one only where every run may get a daemon. Default false.

prebuild_image.description: The name of the image of images a prebuild from a run code runs in, behind the wall of its run: one with docker true and a runtime, such as Qory's prebuild image under sysbox-runc. Default none: such a prebuild stops before anything is fetched.

images_allow.description: Where a run's image may come from when the run's policy, the server's signed run configuration or --policy, names one by a reference pinned by digest: the prefixes of the references the machine runs, in lower case and up to a whole part of a reference, such as a registry, a name or a path ending in a slash, or a name and its @. An image by reference starts under the default image's runtime, so a list needs image or --image. Default none: a run whose policy names an image by reference is refused.

command.description: The program the adapter runs, such as podman. Default docker.

helper.description: The absolute path of a static Linux build of qory, mounted read-only into the container as the relay, the hook forwarder and what starts the daemon of an image with docker: true. Default this binary, which only a Linux machine can use.

env.description: Names of variables of qory run's environment that go into the container, such as the model credential. Values are never written here. Nothing else of the environment goes in.

user.description: The uid:gid the container runs as. Default qory run's, so the checkout's files keep their owner. Root is refused; a machine where qory runs as root sets another.

mounts.description: What the container sees of this machine beside the checkout and the composed home, each at the same path as on the machine: an absolute path, with :ro after it for one the container cannot change. --mount adds to them. A socket, or a directory containing a container runtime's, is refused.

cpus.description: How many processors' worth of time the container gets, a decimal number. Default the engine's.

memory.description: The most memory the container gets: a number of bytes with an optional unit of b, k, m or g. Default the engine's.

pids_limit.description: The most processes and threads in the container. Default the engine's.

shm_size.description: The size of /dev/shm in the container, written as memory is. A browser needs more than an engine's default.

ca_env.description: The variables that point a program at the bundle of authorities it trusts, the image's or this machine's and the run's, when an authority is made for the run: in the container, or on this machine for a run without a wall. Default SSL_CERT_FILE, GIT_SSL_CAINFO, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, AWS_CA_BUNDLE.

setup.description: Where a run's setup commands run before the agent starts, for a run from a control plane whose repositories qory fetches: outside, in a separate container of the run's image on the wall's network, or inside, in the agent's container. Default outside.

engine_proxy_file.description: The absolute path of the file that contains the container engine's proxy setting, which the machine's start unit writes: one JSON object, {"version": 1, "address": "127.0.0.1:3129", "password": "<43 characters of base64url>"}, owned by the user qory runs as, mode 0400 or 0600. A walled run's image is then pulled through the run's proxy. Default none: the engine pulls over the machine's network.

hostForm.description: A host of egress.allow, egress.deny or egress.paths as Forager reads a policy's: a *. suffix, or a host whose last label is neither all digits nor 0x followed by hex digits or none, or an IPv4 address in canonical form, four decimal parts of 0 to 255 with no leading zero.
